content: EPF stands for Employees' Provident Fund, a retirement savings scheme for employees in India.
The Employees' Provident Fund is managed by the Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO).
EPF helps employees save a portion of their salary for retirement.
Both employer and employee contribute to the EPF account every month.
The standard EPF contribution is 12 percent of the employee's basic salary.
EPF applies to organizations that have 20 or more employees.
Employees earning below a certain threshold are mandatorily enrolled in EPF.
EPF accounts earn interest annually as declared by the government.
Employees can check their EPF balance online using the UAN portal.
UAN stands for Universal Account Number, which links multiple EPF accounts.
An employee has only one UAN throughout their career.
EPF contributions are deducted directly from the employee's salary.
Employers are responsible for depositing EPF contributions into the employee's account.
EPF funds can be withdrawn partially under certain conditions.
Employees can withdraw EPF funds after retirement.
Partial withdrawal of EPF is allowed for medical emergencies.
EPF can also be withdrawn for higher education expenses.
Employees can withdraw EPF for marriage-related expenses.
Housing-related withdrawals are allowed under EPF rules.
Employees can transfer EPF accounts when they change jobs.
EPF transfer can be done online using the UAN portal.
KYC details must be updated to access EPF services online.
KYC includes Aadhaar, PAN, and bank account details.
EPF withdrawals may be taxable under certain conditions.
If EPF is withdrawn before five years, tax may be applicable.
EPF interest is tax-free if certain conditions are met.
Employees can nominate beneficiaries for their EPF account.
Nomination ensures smooth transfer of funds in case of death.
EPF passbook shows all transactions in the account.
The EPF passbook can be downloaded from the official portal.
EPF provides financial security after retirement.
Employees can update personal details through the EPFO portal.
Employers must comply with EPF regulations set by the government.
Late EPF contributions may result in penalties for employers.
EPF scheme also includes pension benefits under EPS.
EPS stands for Employees' Pension Scheme.
A portion of employer contribution goes to EPS.
Employees become eligible for pension after meeting criteria.
EPF withdrawals can be done through online claim submission.
Online claims are processed faster than offline submissions.
